name: Commercial Property Insurance
definition: Commercial property insurance pays for direct physical loss of or damage to a business's buildings and business personal property caused by a covered cause of loss. This page is general information about how specific published forms are written. It is not legal advice, it is not a coverage determination, and it does not decide whether any particular loss is covered. Whether a loss is covered is decided by the insurer on the policy actually issued and the facts of the claim, and disputes about that are legal questions for a lawyer. In the common ISO structure, the property insured is described in one form and the perils are supplied by a second form: the Building And Personal Property Coverage Form CP 00 10 10 12 insures Building, Your Business Personal Property and Personal Property Of Others as separately scheduled coverages, and that form states that Covered Property means the types of property described in its section A.1 and limited in its section A.2 Property Not Covered, and only if a Limit Of Insurance is shown in the Declarations for that type of property [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. A causes of loss form sets what counts as a Covered Cause of Loss; the one read for this page is CP 10 30 09 17, which states that when Special is shown in the Declarations, Covered Causes of Loss means direct physical loss unless the loss is excluded or limited in the policy [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Loss of income is not covered by CP 00 10 10 12. Business income is written as its own coverage form, CP 00 30 10 12, separate from the Building And Personal Property Coverage Form, with its own limit of insurance, its own coinsurance condition and its own definitions [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. Several provisions of CP 00 10 10 12 bear on how much is paid on a covered loss. The main ones, and this is not the whole form, are the Limit of Insurance shown in the Declarations for the affected property; the section D Deductible; the Coinsurance Additional Condition, which states that the insurer will not pay the full amount of a loss where the value of Covered Property at the time of loss times the coinsurance percentage shown in the Declarations is greater than the Limit of Insurance for that property; and the Valuation loss condition, which sets actual cash value as of the time of loss as the default except as its own subparagraphs b. through e. provide [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. The section G Optional Coverages, which apply only where shown as applicable in the Declarations, change several of those, and the section C Limitations in the causes of loss form and the sublimits inside the Additional Coverages and Coverage Extensions bear on the figure as well [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12][S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Everything below describes CP 00 10 10 12, CP 10 30 09 17 and CP 00 30 10 12 as published. Edition dates, state variants and carrier forms differ, so read the forms actually attached to the policy.
protects: Buildings and structures, including completed additions, permanently installed fixtures, machinery and equipment, as described in the Building coverage of CP 00 10 10 12, insured only if a Limit Of Insurance for Building is shown in the Declarations and only as limited by that form's A.2 Property Not Covered [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]

Business personal property such as furniture, fixtures, machinery, equipment and stock, insured as Your Business Personal Property under CP 00 10 10 12, which that form describes as property located in or on the described building or structure or in the open, or in a vehicle, within 100 feet of the building or structure or of the described premises, whichever distance is greater [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]

Property of others in the insured's care, custody or control, insured as Personal Property Of Others under CP 00 10 10 12, which that form limits to such property located in or on the described building or structure or in the open, or in a vehicle, within 100 feet of the described premises [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]

A lender's interest in buildings or structures, through the Mortgageholders Additional Condition at F.2 of CP 00 10 10 12, which by its terms pays covered loss of or damage to buildings or structures to each mortgageholder shown in the Declarations in their order of precedence [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]
Earnings and continuing normal operating expenses after a suspension of operations, where CP 00 30 10 12 Business Income coverage is purchased and its trigger is met [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]
The extra costs of continuing to operate after a loss, through the Extra Expense coverage in CP 00 30 10 12 [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]

commonlyCovers.item: Specified (named) perils, where the causes of loss form lists what is insured against
commonlyCovers.note: CDI describes specified perils as consisting of a list of each peril to be insured against, such as fire, explosion, windstorm and vandalism [S:ca-cdi-commercial-insurance-guide]. That is a regulator's general description of the specified perils approach, not the text of any form. The only causes of loss form read for this page is CP 10 30 09 17, which is the special form rather than a named perils form; no ISO basic or broad causes of loss form was reviewed here. Which causes of loss form is attached, and what it lists, is what governs, so read the form on the policy.

commonlyCovers.item: Open perils, under the Causes Of Loss - Special Form
commonlyCovers.note: CP 10 30 09 17 states that when Special is shown in the Declarations, Covered Causes of Loss means direct physical loss unless the loss is excluded or limited in the policy [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. CDI describes open perils coverage as covering all losses unless they are specifically excluded [S:ca-cdi-commercial-insurance-guide]. That structure is broader than a list of named perils, but it is not all-risk in the plain-English sense, because CP 10 30 09 17 runs sections A through G and devotes section B to exclusions and section C to limitations [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. This describes CP 10 30 09 17 only; read the causes of loss form attached to the policy.

commonlyCovers.item: Business income loss during the period of restoration
commonlyCovers.note: CP 00 30 10 12 states that the insurer will pay for the actual loss of Business Income the insured sustains due to the necessary suspension of its operations during the period of restoration, and that the suspension must be caused by direct physical loss of or damage to property at premises described in the Declarations for which a Business Income Limit Of Insurance is shown [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. That form defines Business Income as Net Income, meaning net profit or loss before income taxes that would have been earned or incurred, plus continuing normal operating expenses incurred, including payroll [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. This describes CP 00 30 10 12 only; read the business income form attached to the policy.

CP 00 30 10 12 defines Extra Expense as necessary expenses incurred during the period of restoration that the insured would not have incurred if there had been no direct physical loss or damage to property caused by or resulting from a Covered Cause of Loss [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. Under that form, the period of restoration begins immediately after the time of direct physical loss or damage for Extra Expense Coverage, with no 72-hour wait [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. This describes CP 00 30 10 12 only; read the form attached to the policy.

Under CP 00 30 10 12, coverage may be written as Business Income Including Rental Value, or as Rental Value only, depending on which option is selected in the Declarations, which matters where the loss is rent rather than operating profit [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. That form's definition of Suspension also covers the case where part or all of the described premises is rendered untenantable, where Rental Value coverage applies [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. This describes CP 00 30 10 12 only; read the form attached to the policy.

commonlyCovers.item: Additional coverages and coverage extensions in the property form
commonlyCovers.note: CP 00 10 10 12 carries Additional Coverages at A.4 and Coverage Extensions at A.5 [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. The Coverage Extensions are not automatic: that form states that, except as otherwise provided, they apply to property located in or on the described building or in the open, or in a vehicle, within 100 feet of the described premises, and that the insured may extend the insurance as described only if a coinsurance percentage of 80 percent or more, or a Value Reporting period symbol, is shown in the Declarations [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Those Additional Coverages and Extensions have their own limits and conditions inside the form, so read the specific amounts printed in CP 00 10 10 12 and in the Declarations rather than assuming a standard figure. This describes CP 00 10 10 12 only.

commonlyCovers.item: Collapse, and limited coverage for fungus, wet rot, dry rot and bacteria, as additional coverages
commonlyCovers.note: In CP 10 30 09 17, collapse appears at section D as Additional Coverage - Collapse, and that form states the coverage applies only to an abrupt collapse as described and limited in D.1 through D.7 and that it will not increase the Limits of Insurance provided in the Coverage Part [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Section E is Additional Coverage - Limited Coverage For Fungus, Wet Rot, Dry Rot And Bacteria, which the form says applies only where the fungus, wet or dry rot or bacteria result from a specified cause of loss other than fire or lightning, or from flood where the Flood Coverage Endorsement applies, occurring during the policy period, and only if all reasonable means were used to save and preserve the property from further damage at the time of and after that occurrence [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. That form limits the coverage described at E.2 to $15,000 as the most it will pay for the total of all such loss or damage taking place in a 12-month period, and states the Limited Coverage does not increase the applicable Limit of Insurance [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Neither is an open-ended peril; each is a defined additional coverage with its own conditions. This describes CP 10 30 09 17 only; read the form attached to the policy.

commonlyExcludes.note: In CP 10 30 09 17, exclusion B.1.b Earth Movement covers earthquake including tremors and aftershocks, landslide, mine subsidence, earth sinking other than sinkhole collapse, rising or shifting, and volcanic eruption, explosion or effusion [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. The carve-out of sinkhole collapse from b.(4) matters, because sinkhole collapse is one of the specified causes of loss defined at G.2 of that form [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. The exceptions are not uniform across that list. The form states that if Earth Movement as described in b.(1) through (4) results in fire or explosion, the insurer will pay for the loss or damage caused by that fire or explosion; separately, it states that if volcanic eruption, explosion or effusion under b.(5) results in fire, building glass breakage or Volcanic Action, the insurer will pay for the loss or damage caused by that fire, building glass breakage or Volcanic Action [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Building glass breakage is therefore an exception to the volcanic paragraph, not to earthquake or landslide. The form defines Volcanic Action inside that exclusion, as direct loss or damage resulting from the eruption of a volcano caused by airborne volcanic blast or airborne shock waves, ash, dust or particulate matter, or lava flow, treats all volcanic eruptions within any 168-hour period as a single occurrence, and states that Volcanic Action does not include the cost to remove ash, dust or particulate matter that does not cause direct physical loss or damage to the described property [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. The form also states that the Earth Movement exclusion applies regardless of whether any of b.(1) through (5) is caused by an act of nature or is otherwise caused [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. CDI likewise describes earth movement including earthquake as one of two common perils excluded under open perils coverage [S:ca-cdi-commercial-insurance-guide]. Whether earthquake coverage can be added by endorsement or requires a separate placement, and on what terms and deductible, is a carrier underwriting decision. This describes CP 10 30 09 17 only; read the form attached to the policy.

In CP 10 30 09 17, exclusion B.1.g Water removes flood, surface water, waves including tidal wave and tsunami, tides, tidal water, overflow of any body of water or spray from any of these whether or not driven by wind; mudslide or mudflow; water that backs up or overflows or is otherwise discharged from a sewer, drain, sump, sump pump or related equipment; water under the ground surface pressing on or flowing or seeping through foundations, walls, floors, paved surfaces, basements, doors, windows or other openings; and waterborne material moved by that water [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. The form states that this exclusion applies regardless of whether any of paragraphs (1) through (5) is caused by an act of nature or is otherwise caused, and gives as an example the failure, in whole or in part and for any reason, of a dam, levee, seawall or other boundary or containment system to contain the water [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. The exception is narrower than it is sometimes described: the form states that if any of paragraphs (1) through (5) results in fire, explosion or sprinkler leakage, the insurer will pay for the loss or damage caused by that fire, explosion or sprinkler leakage, and it qualifies the sprinkler leakage branch with the parenthetical if sprinkler leakage is a Covered Cause of Loss [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. There is no defined term Water in that form: section G Definitions of CP 10 30 09 17 contains exactly two defined terms, Fungus and Specified causes of loss, and water damage is defined only inside the Specified causes of loss definition at G.2.c [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. CDI describes flood as one of two common perils excluded under open perils coverage [S:ca-cdi-commercial-insurance-guide]. This describes CP 10 30 09 17 only; read the form attached to the policy.

In CP 10 30 09 17, exclusion B.1.a Ordinance Or Law removes the enforcement of or compliance with any ordinance or law regulating the construction, use or repair of any property, or requiring the tearing down of any property including the cost of removing its debris, and states that it applies whether the loss results from an ordinance enforced even if the property has not been damaged, or from increased costs incurred to comply with an ordinance in the course of construction, repair, renovation, remodeling or demolition following a physical loss [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. CP 00 30 10 12 has a parallel carve-out: the period of restoration in that form does not include any increased period required due to the enforcement of or compliance with any ordinance or law that regulates the construction, use or repair, or requires the tearing down, of any property [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. These notes describe CP 10 30 09 17 and CP 00 30 10 12 only; read the forms attached to the policy.

commonlyExcludes.item: Wear and tear, rust, corrosion, decay and other gradual deterioration
commonlyExcludes.note: Exclusion B.2.d of CP 10 30 09 17 runs d.(1) through d.(7) and excludes loss or damage caused by or resulting from: (1) wear and tear; (2) rust or other corrosion, decay, deterioration, hidden or latent defect or any quality in property that causes it to damage or destroy itself; (3) smog; (4) settling, cracking, shrinking or expansion; (5) nesting or infestation, or discharge or release of waste products or secretions, by insects, birds, rodents or other animals; (6) mechanical breakdown, including rupture or bursting caused by centrifugal force; and (7) dampness or dryness of atmosphere, changes in or extremes of temperature, and marring or scratching, each as to personal property only [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Two exceptions inside that paragraph matter and are easy to miss. The mechanical breakdown subparagraph states that if mechanical breakdown results in elevator collision, the insurer will pay for the loss or damage caused by that elevator collision [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. And the paragraph closes with a general ensuing-loss exception: if an excluded cause of loss listed in 2.d.(1) through (7) results in a specified cause of loss or building glass breakage, the insurer will pay for the loss or damage caused by that specified cause of loss or building glass breakage [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Faulty or inadequate maintenance is not in B.2 at all; it appears separately at B.3.c(4), and section B.3 carries its own exception stating that if an excluded cause of loss listed in 3.a. through 3.c. results in a Covered Cause of Loss, the insurer will pay for the loss or damage caused by that Covered Cause of Loss [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. So under this form deterioration and faulty maintenance are excluded as causes, but what they lead to can still be paid where one of those stated exceptions applies. That is a statement about CP 10 30 09 17, not a universal rule of the property line; read the causes of loss form attached to the policy.

commonlyExcludes.item: Dishonest or criminal acts by the insured or its employees
commonlyExcludes.note: Section B.2.h of CP 10 30 09 17 excludes dishonest or criminal act, including theft, by the named insured, any of its partners, members, officers, managers, employees including temporary employees and leased workers, directors, trustees or authorized representatives, whether acting alone or in collusion with each other or with any other party; the same exclusion carries a second branch covering theft by any person to whom the insured entrusts the property for any purpose, whether acting alone or in collusion with any other party [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. The exclusion states that it applies whether or not the act occurs during the insured's normal hours of operation, and it carries a stated exception: it does not apply to acts of destruction by the insured's employees, including temporary employees and leased workers, or authorized representatives, but theft by those same people is not covered [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. So under this form employee vandalism can be a different question from employee theft. Coverage for employee theft would have to come from something other than this causes of loss form. This describes CP 10 30 09 17 only; read the form attached to the policy.

commonlyExcludes.item: Fungus, wet rot, dry rot and bacteria
commonlyExcludes.note: Exclusion B.1.h of CP 10 30 09 17 removes presence, growth, proliferation, spread or any activity of fungus, wet or dry rot or bacteria, and states that the exclusion does not apply where those result from fire or lightning, or to the extent coverage is provided in the Additional Coverage at section E, Limited Coverage For Fungus, Wet Rot, Dry Rot And Bacteria, and that second branch is itself qualified in the form to loss or damage by a cause of loss other than fire or lightning [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. The form also states that if fungus, wet or dry rot or bacteria result in a specified cause of loss, the insurer will pay for the loss or damage caused by that specified cause of loss [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. This describes CP 10 30 09 17 only; read the form attached to the policy.

commonlyExcludes.item: Governmental action, nuclear hazard, utility services, and war and military action
commonlyExcludes.note: These are exclusions B.1.c through B.1.f of CP 10 30 09 17 [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Three of the four carry stated exceptions that a reader must not drop, and the fourth, War And Military Action at B.1.f, carries none in that form [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. The Governmental Action exclusion at B.1.c removes seizure or destruction of property by order of governmental authority, but the form then states that the insurer will pay for loss or damage caused by or resulting from acts of destruction ordered by governmental authority and taken at the time of a fire to prevent its spread, if the fire would be covered under the Coverage Part [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. The Nuclear Hazard exclusion at B.1.d removes nuclear reaction or radiation, or radioactive contamination, however caused, but the form then states that if nuclear reaction or radiation, or radioactive contamination, results in fire, the insurer will pay for the loss or damage caused by that fire [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. The Utility Services exclusion at B.1.e removes the failure of power, communication, water or other utility service supplied to the described premises, however caused, where the failure originates away from the described premises or involves equipment used to supply the service from a source away from the premises, and it also excludes loss caused by a surge of power that would not have occurred but for an event causing a failure of power [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. The form states that failure of any utility service includes lack of sufficient capacity and reduction in supply, and that communication services include but are not limited to service relating to Internet access or access to any electronic, cellular or satellite network [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. It excepts a Covered Cause of Loss resulting from that failure or surge [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. This describes CP 10 30 09 17 only; read the form attached to the policy.

commonlyExcludes.item: Neglect to protect property after a loss
commonlyExcludes.note: Section B.2.m of CP 10 30 09 17 excludes neglect of an insured to use all reasonable means to save and preserve property from further damage at and after the time of loss [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Under this form, post-loss mitigation therefore bears directly on what is payable. That is a statement about CP 10 30 09 17; read the causes of loss form attached to the policy.

commonlyExcludes.item: Business income where the form's physical damage trigger is not met
commonlyExcludes.note: Whether any particular event triggers business income coverage is a claim question decided by the insurer on the policy issued and the facts, and contested triggers are legal questions for a lawyer. This page states only what the form requires. CP 00 30 10 12 states that the suspension of operations must be caused by direct physical loss of or damage to property at premises described in the Declarations for which a Business Income Limit Of Insurance is shown, and that the loss or damage must be caused by or result from a Covered Cause of Loss [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. It also defines Suspension as the slowdown or cessation of business activities, or the described premises being rendered untenantable where Rental Value coverage applies [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. This describes CP 00 30 10 12 only; read the form attached to the policy.

commonlyExcludes.item: The section B.1 exclusions carry a lead-in about contributing causes
commonlyExcludes.note: The section B.1 exclusions in CP 10 30 09 17 are introduced by language stating that the insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused directly or indirectly by any of the listed causes, and that such loss or damage is excluded regardless of any other cause or event that contributes concurrently or in any sequence to the loss [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. That sentence is the wording of the clause and is all this page states about it. What effect the clause has on any particular loss is not determined by the form text and is not decided here; take it to a lawyer. This describes CP 10 30 09 17 only; read the form attached to the policy.

limitsAndDeductibles: Limits of insurance are scheduled separately in the Declarations for Building, Your Business Personal Property and Personal Property Of Others under CP 00 10 10 12 [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].

Section D Deductible of CP 00 10 10 12 applies in any one occurrence of loss or damage: the form first reduces the amount of loss if required by the Coinsurance Condition or the Agreed Value Optional Coverage, pays nothing if the adjusted amount is less than or equal to the deductible, and otherwise subtracts the deductible and pays the resulting amount or the Limit of Insurance, whichever is less [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. That section also states that where the occurrence involves loss to more than one item of Covered Property and separate Limits of Insurance apply, the losses will not be combined in determining application of the deductible, but the deductible will be applied only once per occurrence [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. If a policy shows a percentage or named-storm deductible, that provision does not come from this base form; find the endorsement or Declarations entry that creates it and read its own wording.

Coinsurance is Additional Condition F.1 of CP 00 10 10 12 and applies only if a coinsurance percentage is shown in the Declarations [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. It states that the insurer will not pay the full amount of any loss if the value of Covered Property at the time of loss times the coinsurance percentage shown in the Declarations is greater than the Limit of Insurance for that property [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].

The coinsurance calculation in CP 00 10 10 12 multiplies the value of Covered Property at the time of loss by the coinsurance percentage, divides the Limit of Insurance by that figure, multiplies the total amount of loss before the application of any deductible by the result, and then subtracts the deductible; the form states that it will pay the amount so determined or the Limit of Insurance, whichever is less, and that for the remainder the insured will either have to rely on other insurance or absorb the loss itself [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Because the shortfall is applied to the amount of loss, it reaches partial losses and not only total losses. That form also states that where one Limit of Insurance applies to two or more separate items, the Coinsurance condition applies to the total of all property to which the limit applies [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. CDI describes coinsurance as a clause defining the amount of each loss the company pays according to the amount of insurance carried divided by the amount of insurance required, and warns that a policyholder can be subject to a monetary penalty at the time of a loss where a building is not insured to value [S:ca-cdi-commercial-insurance-guide].

The Agreed Value Optional Coverage in section G of CP 00 10 10 12 states that the Additional Condition, Coinsurance, does not apply to Covered Property to which that Optional Coverage applies [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. The same paragraph carries a second clause that is easy to drop: the form states that it will pay no more for loss of or damage to that property than the proportion that the Limit of Insurance under the Coverage Part for the property bears to the Agreed Value shown for it in the Declarations [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. The Optional Coverage also applies only to loss or damage occurring on or after its effective date and before the earlier of the Agreed Value expiration date shown in the Declarations or the policy expiration date [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. CDI, describing the agreed value approach generally rather than this form, says it waives any coinsurance penalty and pays 100 percent of the stated amount [S:ca-cdi-commercial-insurance-guide]; on CP 00 10 10 12 the proportional clause above is what the form actually prints, so read the form rather than the general description.

CP 00 30 10 12 carries its own Coinsurance Additional Condition, measured against the coinsurance percentage times the sum of Net Income and operating expenses including payroll that would have been earned or incurred for the 12 months following the inception or last previous anniversary date of the policy, whichever is later [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. That is a forward-looking figure under the form, so a worksheet built only on last year's actuals is measuring something different from what the condition measures.
The Maximum Period Of Indemnity and Monthly Limit Of Indemnity Optional Coverages in CP 00 30 10 12 each state that the Additional Condition, Coinsurance, does not apply [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12].

Business income under CP 00 30 10 12 uses a waiting period rather than a dollar deductible: the period of restoration begins 72 hours after the time of direct physical loss or damage for Business Income Coverage and immediately after that time for Extra Expense Coverage [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. That waiting period is a provision of this edition of this form; other editions and carrier forms can differ, so check what is attached.

Valuation defaults to actual cash value as of the time of loss or damage under loss condition E.7 of CP 00 10 10 12, and that form states the default applies except as provided in subparagraphs b., c., d. and e. of that condition, which are four stated exceptions rather than one [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Subparagraph b. pays the cost of building repairs or replacement where the Limit of Insurance for Building satisfies the Coinsurance condition and the cost to repair or replace the damaged building property is $2,500 or less; that exception itself excludes the increased cost attributable to enforcement of or compliance with any ordinance or law regulating the construction, use or repair of any property, and the form directs that awnings or floor coverings, appliances for refrigerating, ventilating, cooking, dishwashing or laundering, and outdoor equipment or furniture be valued at actual cash value even when attached to the building [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Subparagraph c. values Stock the insured has sold but not delivered at the selling price less discounts and expenses it otherwise would have had; subparagraph d. values glass at the cost of replacement with safety-glazing material if required by law; and subparagraph e. values tenants' improvements and betterments in three branches, not two: at actual cash value if repairs are made promptly; at a stated proportion of original cost, computed from the days remaining on the lease, if they are not; and at nothing if others pay for the repairs or replacement [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].

Replacement Cost is Optional Coverage G.3 of CP 00 10 10 12, applies only if shown as applicable in the Declarations, and replaces Actual Cash Value in the Valuation loss condition [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. That Optional Coverage states it does not apply to four things: personal property of others; contents of a residence; works of art, antiques or rare articles including etchings, pictures, statuary, marbles, bronzes, porcelains and bric-a-brac; and Stock, unless the Including Stock option is shown in the Declarations [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. The Stock carve-out matters for retail, wholesale and distribution risks.

Under CP 00 10 10 12, the insurer will not pay on a replacement cost basis until the lost or damaged property is actually repaired or replaced, and unless the repair or replacement is made as soon as reasonably possible after the loss or damage [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. The form also lets the insured claim on an actual cash value basis first and still claim the additional replacement cost amount if it gives notice of intent to do so within 180 days after the loss or damage [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Because the form conditions payment on the repair or replacement having actually been made, the replacement cost portion under CP 00 10 10 12 is payable after that work rather than before it. Tenants' improvements and betterments have their own branch: that Optional Coverage states that where those two conditions are not met, tenants' improvements and betterments are valued as a proportion of original cost as set out in the Valuation loss condition, and that the insurer will not pay for loss or damage to them at all if others pay for the repairs or replacement [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].

Replacement cost under CP 00 10 10 12 is also capped and carved out. That Optional Coverage states the insurer will not pay more on a replacement cost basis than the least of the Limit of Insurance applicable to the lost or damaged property, the cost to replace it with other property of comparable material and quality used for the same purpose, or the amount actually spent that is necessary to repair or replace it, and that if a building is rebuilt at a new premises the replacement cost figure is limited to what would have been incurred had it been rebuilt at the original premises [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. It further states that the cost of repair or replacement does not include the increased cost attributable to enforcement of or compliance with any ordinance or law regulating the construction, use or repair of any property [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].

Inflation Guard is Optional Coverage G.2 of CP 00 10 10 12 and automatically increases the Limit of Insurance for property to which it applies by the annual percentage shown in the Declarations [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. That increase accrues over the year rather than landing all at once: the form computes the amount of increase as the Limit of Insurance in effect at the most recent policy inception, anniversary or limit-amending change, times the annual percentage shown in the Declarations, times the number of days since that date divided by 365 [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].

endorsements.note: Addresses the B.1.a Ordinance Or Law exclusion in CP 10 30 09 17 and the parallel ordinance or law carve-out from the period of restoration in CP 00 30 10 12 [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17][S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. No ordinance or law endorsement was reviewed for this page, so what any particular one covers, and with what limits, comes from that endorsement's own wording.

endorsements.item: Earthquake and flood coverage or separate policies
endorsements.note: Needed because CP 10 30 09 17 excludes Earth Movement at B.1.b and Water at B.1.g [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17], and because CDI describes earth movement including earthquake and flood as two common perils excluded under open perils coverage [S:ca-cdi-commercial-insurance-guide]. Whether a given risk can get earthquake or flood coverage by endorsement or by separate placement, on what terms, and whether that placement is admitted or surplus line, are carrier and broker decisions on the individual risk; no source cited on this page speaks to that, and no earthquake or flood endorsement or standalone policy form was reviewed here.

Under CP 00 10 10 12, the Agreed Value Optional Coverage suspends the Coinsurance Additional Condition for the Covered Property to which it applies, and the form states that if the expiration date shown for it in the Declarations is not extended, Coinsurance is reinstated and the Optional Coverage expires [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. It therefore has to be maintained at each renewal to keep operating. Suspending coinsurance is not the same as removing every proportional reduction: the same paragraph states that the insurer will pay no more for loss of or damage to that property than the proportion that the Limit of Insurance for the property bears to the Agreed Value shown for it in the Declarations [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. This describes CP 00 10 10 12 only.

endorsements.item: Replacement Cost, including the extension to personal property of others
endorsements.note: Replacement Cost is an Optional Coverage in CP 00 10 10 12 that must be shown as applicable in the Declarations, and by its own terms it does not apply to personal property of others, contents of a residence, works of art, antiques or rare articles, or Stock unless the Including Stock option is shown [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. That form carries a separate Extension Of Replacement Cost To Personal Property Of Others Optional Coverage at G.4, which the form says may be shown as applicable only if the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage is itself shown as applicable, and which deletes the personal-property-of-others carve-out while leaving the rest of the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage in force [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Under that Extension, where an item of personal property of others is subject to a written contract governing the insured's liability for loss or damage to it, valuation of that item is based on the amount for which the insured is liable under that contract, but the form caps that at the lesser of the replacement cost of the property or the applicable Limit of Insurance, and that cap is part of the same sentence [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. This describes CP 00 10 10 12 only.

endorsements.item: Business income options: Maximum Period Of Indemnity, Monthly Limit Of Indemnity, Business Income Agreed Value, Extended Period Of Indemnity
endorsements.note: These are the four Optional Coverages in CP 00 30 10 12 [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. Extended Period Of Indemnity matters because the base period of restoration in that form ends on the earlier of the date the property should be repaired, rebuilt or replaced with reasonable speed and similar quality, or the date business is resumed at a new permanent location, rather than when revenue recovers [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. This describes CP 00 30 10 12 only.

endorsements.item: Utility services, direct damage and time element
endorsements.note: CP 10 30 09 17 excludes Utility Services at B.1.e, so off-premises power, water or communication failure falls outside that form's covered causes of loss except where it results in a Covered Cause of Loss [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Any coverage for that exposure has to come from an endorsement. No utility services endorsement was reviewed for this page.

endorsements.item: Equipment breakdown, spoilage, and dependent property (contingent business income)
endorsements.note: CP 00 30 10 12 requires the suspension to be caused by direct physical loss of or damage to property at premises described in the Declarations, so damage at a supplier's or customer's premises is outside that trigger unless something else supplies it [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. No dependent property, equipment breakdown or spoilage endorsement was reviewed for this page; read the endorsement attached to the policy.

Inflation Guard is an Optional Coverage in CP 00 10 10 12 that automatically increases the Limit of Insurance for property to which it applies by the annual percentage shown in the Declarations, computed by that form as the applicable limit times that percentage times the number of days since the beginning of the current policy year or the most recent limit-amending change, divided by 365 [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Because the Coinsurance condition in that form measures the Limit of Insurance against the value of Covered Property at the time of loss, a limit that moves with values behaves differently under that calculation than a static one [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. This describes CP 00 10 10 12 only.

relatedPolicies: Business Owners Policy (BOP), which CDI describes as a combination commercial policy that covers property, general liability and business interruption [S:ca-cdi-commercial-insurance-guide]
Commercial general liability, which under CG 00 01 04 13 covers third-party bodily injury and property damage rather than the insured's own property [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]
Business income and extra expense, written as its own coverage form with its own limit of insurance, coinsurance condition and definitions [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]
Standalone earthquake and flood coverage, given the Earth Movement and Water exclusions in CP 10 30 09 17 [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]

Equipment breakdown, crime and fidelity, inland marine, builders risk and cargo coverage, for property and causes that CP 00 10 10 12 and CP 10 30 09 17 do not reach [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12][S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]

Difference in conditions placements and surplus line property markets. CDI states that a surplus line company can only be accessed through a specially licensed broker, that it has limited jurisdiction over the operation of surplus line insurers, and that the California Insurance Guarantee Association does not apply to surplus line insurers [S:ca-cdi-commercial-insurance-guide]
underwritingInputs: Construction type, year built, number of stories, square footage and occupancy of each building
Age and condition of roof, electrical, plumbing and HVAC, and the dates of any updates
Protection information: sprinklers, alarms, distance to hydrant and responding fire station, and public protection classification

A statement of values supporting the Building and business personal property limits, since under CP 00 10 10 12 the Limit of Insurance drives both the amount recoverable and the Coinsurance calculation [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]

A business income worksheet showing net income and continuing operating expenses including payroll for the 12 months following inception, which is the period the Coinsurance Additional Condition in CP 00 30 10 12 measures [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]

Expected time to rebuild, permit and code exposure, and any long-lead equipment, all of which bear on the period of restoration in CP 00 30 10 12 and on the ordinance or law exclusion in CP 10 30 09 17 [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12][S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]
Catastrophe exposure: distance to coast, brush and wildfire exposure, flood zone and seismic exposure
Loss history, typically several years of currently valued loss runs
Whether the insured is owner or tenant, and what the lease requires the tenant to insure

Which causes of loss form is being requested, and which coinsurance percentage and valuation basis apply. CDI describes the specified perils and open perils approaches and the actual cash value, agreed value and replacement cost valuation approaches [S:ca-cdi-commercial-insurance-guide]
Lender requirements, including mortgageholder wording, which CP 00 10 10 12 addresses in its Mortgageholders Additional Condition [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]

This list describes information commonly requested in practice. It is common practice rather than a legal or filed requirement, and what any particular insurer asks for, and whether it offers terms at all, is a carrier underwriting decision

exposures.item: Direct physical loss to a building or to business personal property
exposures.note: The building and personal property coverage form is the document that defines what property is covered and on what basis [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. What counts as covered property, and what is excluded from it, is read there rather than assumed.

exposures.item: Loss of income while the property is being repaired
exposures.note: Business income and extra expense is addressed by its own form rather than by the property form [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12], so the time element and the physical damage are two separate grants with their own conditions.

exposures.item: A cause of loss the policy does not name
exposures.note: The causes of loss form determines which perils are in scope [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. A named-peril and a special-form policy answer this exposure differently, and which one is in force is on the declarations page.

exposures.item: Underinsurance discovered at the time of loss
exposures.note: California law addresses the measure of indemnity and the effect of the amount of insurance carried [S:ca-ins-code-530]. A limit set once and never revisited is the ordinary way this exposure arises.

exposures.item: Liability arising from the same premises, which the property policy does not address
exposures.note: Property and liability are separate coverage parts: the general liability form responds to sums owed as damages because of bodily injury or property damage to others [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13], which is a different question from damage to the insured's own building.

claimMitigation.item: Read the causes of loss form before assuming a peril is covered
claimMitigation.note: Scope is set by the causes of loss form attached to the policy [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17], not by the property form alone. Ask which causes of loss form is in force and read it.

claimMitigation.item: Revisit the limit against current replacement cost, in writing
claimMitigation.note: The statutory measure of indemnity turns in part on the amount of insurance carried [S:ca-ins-code-530]. A written, dated basis for the limit is what makes the figure defensible later.

claimMitigation.item: Confirm business income is actually purchased and on what period
claimMitigation.note: Business income and extra expense sits on its own form [S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12]. Its presence, its limit and its period of restoration are separate from the property limit and are read on that form.

claimMitigation.item: Assemble the underwriting information the market asks for before you need terms
claimMitigation.note: Commercial property submissions ask for construction, occupancy, protection and exposure information [S:ca-cdi-commercial-insurance-guide]. Having it current shortens the conversation and makes gaps visible while there is still time to address them.

stateVariations.note: CDI's Commercial Insurance Guide describes specified perils versus open perils, states that earth movement including earthquake and flood are two common perils excluded under open perils coverage, describes the actual cash value, agreed value and replacement cost valuation approaches, and warns that a policyholder can be subject to a monetary penalty at the time of a loss where a building is not insured to value [S:ca-cdi-commercial-insurance-guide]. CDI also states that after three documented declinations from licensed commercial carriers a business can proceed to the surplus line market, that a surplus line company can only be accessed through a specially licensed broker, that the CDI has limited jurisdiction over the operation of surplus line insurers, and that the California Insurance Guarantee Association, which protects claims with admitted insurers, does not apply to surplus line insurers [S:ca-cdi-commercial-insurance-guide]. On causation, California Insurance Code section 530 states that an insurer is liable for a loss of which a peril insured against was the proximate cause, although a peril not contemplated by the contract may have been a remote cause of the loss, but is not liable for a loss of which the peril insured against was only a remote cause [S:ca-ins-code-530]. That is what the statute says. How it bears on any particular policy wording or loss is a legal question for a lawyer and is not answered anywhere on this page. Nothing on this page determines whether a specific California property is written in the admitted market, placed in the surplus line market, or eligible for any residual market program; those are carrier and broker decisions on the individual risk.

The provisions described on this page are those of CP 00 10 10 12 and CP 00 30 10 12, each carrying the ISO copyright date 2011, and CP 10 30 09 17, carrying the ISO copyright date 2016 [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12][S:iso-cp-00-30-10-12][S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. They describe specific editions of specific forms, not universal policy language. Other editions, state variants and carrier forms exist and can read differently, so read the forms on the policy.
